Analyze a solid circular shaft under torsion only, using small-deformation linear-elastic theory in N–mm–MPa units.
The shaft is solid circular with diameter d = 30 mm and total length L = 1200 mm.
The material is AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76923.1 MPa.
The shaft is fixed (clamped) at x = 0 and free at x = 1200 mm.
A torque T2 = -200000 N·mm is applied at x = 400 mm and a torque T1 = +200000 N·mm is applied at the free end x = 1200 mm.
No transverse forces, bending moments, or axial loads exist; the only loading is the two torques.
Compute the internal torque in each of the two segments: segment A from x = 0 to 400 mm and segment B from x = 400 to 1200 mm.
Determine internal torque per segment using free-body equilibrium starting from the free end.
Calculate the polar moment of inertia J = πd⁴/32 for the solid circular cross-section.
Compute the maximum torsional shear stress in each segment using τ = T·c/J, where c = d/2 = 15 mm.
Compute the angle of twist of each segment using φ = T·L_segment/(J·G) and sum the two segment contributions to obtain the total twist at the free end x = 1200 mm relative to the fixed end.
Present the governing relations: equilibrium of internal torque, τ = T·c/J, and φ = Σ T·L/(J·G), with sign convention consistent with the applied torque signs.
State any additional assumptions explicitly: homogeneous isotropic material, constant circular cross-section, torques applied as concentrated moments at the stated locations, and no stress concentrations at the load application points.
Report the response quantities: internal torque per segment, maximum shear stress per segment (identify the critical segment and location), and the total angle of twist at the free end.
